chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the words of Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'By Allah! A thousand strikes with the sword are easier than death upon a bed.' He said: 'In the Way of Allah.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'A thousand strikes with the sword are easier than death upon a bed' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the comparison in Imam Ali’s saying refers specifically to martyrdom 'in the Way of Allah,' elevating the spiritual status of dying in battle over a peaceful, natural death. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on active struggle (jihad) and the merit of shedding blood for divine cause, as recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on the virtues of martyrdom. The narration underscores that while natural death is not condemned, the voluntary sacrifice in God’s path holds superior reward.
